items.title: Micah Parsons, Josh Jacobs listed as limited in practice again on Monday
items.text: The Packers' injury report for Monday looks a lot like the one they turned in on Sunday.

items.title: Rams upgrade RB Kyren Williams to full participant on Monday's injury report
items.text: While any injury news about the Rams has largely been bad this season, there was a positive development on the team's Monday practice report.

items.title: Marlon Humphrey back with Ravens, Jesse Minter doesn't commit to Week 12 return to lineup
items.text: Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey was back at the team's facility on Monday.

items.title: Bengals activate LB Swayze Bozeman, G Brian Parker from injured reserve
items.text: The Bengals announced a pair of roster moves on Monday afternoon.

items.title: DK Metcalf will not be suspended for actions during Steelers-Eagles
items.text: According to multiple reports, while Metcalf has avoided a suspension, he may still be fined.

items.title: Commanders activate Jacory Croskey-Merritt
items.text: The Commanders have made an addition to their offensive backfield ahead of Monday night's game against the Bengals.

items.title: Giants CB Greg Newsome out multiple weeks with high-ankle sprain
items.text: Giants cornerback Greg Newsome left Sunday's win over the Jaguars with an ankle injury and it will be some time before he will be back in the lineup.

items.title: Vikings "don't necessarily expect" Jordan Addison back this week
items.text: The Vikings didn't have wide receiver Jordan Addison in the lineup for Sunday night's game against the 49ers and his availability for Week 12 came up during head coach Kevin O'Connell's Monday press conference.

items.title: Cardinals fire defensive coordinator Nick Rallis
items.text: Teryl Austin will serve as interim defensive coordinator.

items.title: Super Bowl LXI will be shown in IMAX theaters
items.text: The Super Bowl will be shown on some very big screens this season.

items.title: Rams TE Terrance Ferguson to undergo season-ending ankle surgery
items.text: One of the Rams' young pass-catchers will not be able to return in 2026.

items.title: Shane Steichen says Colts have not shut down Alec Pierce for the season
items.text: A report from NFL Media on Sunday morning indicated that the Colts have decided to pull the plug on hopes that wide receiver Alec Pierce will return to action this season, but it appears to have been premature.

items.title: Terrion Arnold's lawyer seeks sanctions for discovery violation
items.text: Seahawks cornerback Terrion Arnold remains on paid leave with eight felony charges pending in Florida.

items.title: Report: Giants DC Dennard Wilson had a virtual interview for Maryland head coaching job
items.text: Giants defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson has helped the team to a 6-3-1 record so far this season and he's landed on the interview list for a head coaching vacancy on the college level.

items.title: Panthers WR Jalen Coker is not in concussion protocol
items.text: Panthers wide receiver Jalen Coker was checked for a concussion in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game against the Ravens, but head coach Dave Canales had a positive update on his condition on Monday.

items.title: 49ers release WR Brandon Aiyuk
items.text: Aiyuk will next go to waivers.

items.title: Klint Kubiak on Fernando Mendoza: With two starts against two elite defenses, I've seen improvement
items.text: While Fernando Mendoza is still looking for his first win as a starting quarterback, the No. 1 overall pick of this year's draft displayed his considerable potential in Sunday's loss to the Broncos.

items.title: 49ers extend G.M. John Lynch's contract
items.text: In the offseason, the 49ers quietly extended the contract of coach Kyle Shanahan.

items.title: Quinnen Williams: We executed better on defense, but we still gave up 30 points
items.text: The Cowboys defense was under the microscope all week due to the decision to strip defensive coordinator Christian Parker of play-calling duties and hand them to assistant Mike Pettine, but defensive tackle Quinnen Williams pointed to something else playing a leading role in the unit's performance on Sunday.

items.title: Aaron Rodgers calls DK Metcalf's ejection "disappointing," won't comment on message to him
items.text: On certain subjects, Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers doesn't stop talking.

items.title: Steelers' offense is awful in loss to Eagles
items.text: A Philadelphia defense that previously looked like it was packing it in on the season stepped up in a big way today.

items.title: DK Metcalf: I didn't try to poke Cooper DeJean in the eye
items.text: Metcalf was ejected from Sunday's game after an altercation with the Eagles defensive back.

items.title: Mike Vrabel on Drake Maye: We want to give him every opportunity to return at some point
items.text: Drake Maye is going to be out for an extended period after suffering a fractured fibula in the Week 10 loss to the Lions.

items.title: Mike Vrabel says Pats don't plan to add another QB: Tommy DeVito is our starter
items.text: While Drake Maye is going to be out for an extended period — if not the rest of the season — the Patriots are not currently inclined to add quarterback Daniel Jones.

items.title: Falcons waive LB Christian Harris, sign S Jammie Robinson
items.text: The Falcons announced a change to their roster coming out of their bye week.

items.title: Travis Kelce moves past Rob Gronkowski for No. 3 all-time in TD catches by a tight end
items.text: For the first time since Sept. 27, Travis Kelce has gotten back into the end zone.

items.title: Cooper DeJean: DK Metcalf "just missed" poking me in the eye
items.text: Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean says Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf didn’t poke him in the eye on Sunday, but came pretty close.

items.title: Malik Nabers on sideline moment: I was just trying to watch the game
items.text: Late in Sunday's win over the Jaguars, video of the Giants' sideline showed quarterback Jameis Winston trying to restrain receiver Malik Nabers.

items.title: Officials deny Jaguars TD on sensational catch by Parker Washington
items.text: Washington appeared to make a superb touchdown catch, but the officials and the replay office ruled it incomplete.

items.title: Mike Evans TD and Parker Washington non-TD raise more questions about NFL catch rules
items.text: Two big plays on Sunday renewed questions about what is and is not a catch in the NFL.

items.title: Daniel Jones has cleared waivers and is now free to sign with any team.
items.text: - Zachary Krueger

items.title: Quinyon Mitchell (hamstring) did not practice on Monday.
items.text: It was an estimated session. Mitchell talked with reporters after leaving Sunday’s game with the hamstring ailment, implying it wasn’t a super serious injury. Still, on a short week, his status is up in the air. If he were ruled out, it would only help CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens on Thanksgiving. - Rivers McCown

items.title: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is practicing in full ahead of Philadelphia’s Thursday game against the Cowboys.
items.text: We’re expecting the Eagles to force-feed Smith once more after his 57 percent target share on Sunday, leaving him as a plausible WR2 in an elevated matchup against the Cowboys defense. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Will Shipley (foot/illness) was limited in Monday’s practice.
items.text: It was an estimated session and exactly the same listing he had on Friday. As he was practicing on a limited basis before the illness (and before being activated off injured reserve last Saturday), we’ll assume he has a fairly good chance to suit up on Thursday. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Dallas Goedert (shin) was limited in Monday’s practice.
items.text: It’s a new (estimated) listing after his one-catch outing against the Steelers. Goedert was at least set up with a Joe Milton #RevengeGame script against a weak Cowboys defense this week to try to rebound, but it will be hard to rely on him as a streamer TE1 if healthy. We’ll see if he can get to the second part of that statement tomorrow. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Saquon Barkley (neck/illness) was limited in Monday’s practice.
items.text: We described Barkley as leaving the game in the fourth quarter with what “appeared to be a left arm” injury in Sunday’s blurb, it sounds like it may have been a stinger based on the neck listing. A limited (estimated) session is better than a DNP, but Tuesday’s report will loom large for Barkley’s chances of playing against the Cowboys on Thursday. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Micah Parsons (knee) was limited in Monday’s practice.
items.text: Parsons has been limited in each of the Packers’ first two practices to start the week. It’s long been believed that the star pass-rusher could be activated for Wednesday’s game against the Rams, but the team has declined to say whether or not that will come to fruition. We will likely have an official word on Parsons’ Week 12 availability when the Packers release their final injury report on Tuesday. - Zachary Krueger

items.title: Colby Parkinson (ribs) practiced in full on Monday.
items.text: He’s gotten in two full sessions coming off the bye and figures to remain one of the main figures in the Rams’ floating opera of tight end production that they’ll likely be relying on this week sans Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Josh Jacobs (thumb) was limited in Monday’s practice.
items.text: Jacobs has been limited in each of the Packers’ first two practices as they prepare to face the Rams on Wednesday. While a limited session would generally be viewed as an encouraging sign for a player, head coach Matt LaFleur said earlier that he doesn’t expect Jacobs to suit up this week. We will continue to track his status until he receives an official designation for the game, but we’re assuming based on LaFleur’s comments that Jacobs will miss at least one more week. - Zachary Krueger

items.title: Kyren Williams (toe) practiced in full on Monday.
items.text: It’s an upgrade from a limited session on Sunday and we’d be surprised if Williams was placed on the questionable line on Tuesday. - Rivers McCown
